answer: The ivory detector writes to ridge, and meadow reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, which means the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 264 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. Submissions that land within 185 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 6 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
